10-K.summary:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY – Apple Inc. (AAPL), Form 10-K, fiscal year ended September 27, 2025

1. BUSINESS AND REVENUE PERFORMANCE
- Total net sales: $416,161 million (+6%), versus $391,035 million in 2024
- Total gross margin: $195,201 million; gross margin percentage 46.9% (2024: 46.2%)
- Total operating expenses: $62,151 million (+8%); R&D $34,550 million (+10%); SG&A $27,601 million (+6%)
- Provision for income taxes: $20,719 million; effective tax rate 15.6% (2024: 24.1%)
- By product category:
  - iPhone: $209,586 million (+4%), driven by higher sales of Pro models
  - Services: $109,158 million (+14%), driven by advertising, the App Store and cloud services
  - Mac: $33,708 million (+12%)
  - iPad: $28,023 million (+5%)
  - Wearables, Home and Accessories: $35,686 million (-4%)
- By region:
  - Americas: $178,353 million (+7%)
  - Europe: $111,032 million (+10%)
  - Greater China: $64,377 million (-4%), due to lower iPhone sales
  - Japan: $28,703 million (+15%)
  - Rest of Asia Pacific: $33,696 million (+10%)
- Gross margin by type: Services 75.4% (2024: 73.9%) and Products 36.8% (2024: 37.2%)

2. THREE KEY RISKS
- Tariffs and trade disputes (new in 2025): new U.S. Tariffs were announced beginning in the second quarter of 2025, including on imports from China, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam and the EU. Several countries have imposed or threatened reciprocal tariffs. A Section 232 investigation into semiconductors and their derivative products is under way. The ultimate impact remains uncertain. The Company depends on outsourcing partners located primarily in Asia and on single-source suppliers.
- Regulatory and antitrust pressure: the Company is subject to the EU Digital Markets Act, where its compliance plan has been challenged by the Commission. In the U.S., a court order prevents it from imposing any commission or fee on certain App Store purchases. It also faces civil antitrust lawsuits alleging monopolization in smartphone markets, and investigations in Europe and other jurisdictions into App Store terms.
- Dependence on Google search licensing revenue: on September 2, 2025, the D.C. District Court ordered remedies after Google was found to have violated U.S. antitrust laws. The order is subject to further proceedings and appeal. If the remedies initially proposed by the DOJ were imposed, they could materially harm the Company's ability to earn revenue from these licensing arrangements.

4. FINANCIAL RED FLAGS is covered below after strategic changes.

3. STRATEGIC CHANGES
- Product launches during fiscal 2025:
  - iPhone 16e and, in the fourth quarter, iPhone 17, iPhone Air, iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max
  - New MacBook Pro, Mac mini, iMac, MacBook Air and Mac Studio
  - iPad mini, iPad Air and iPad
  - Apple Watch Series 11, SE 3 and Ultra 3, plus AirPods Pro 3
  - Software releases: iOS 26 and the rest of the 26 operating system family
- Capital return: in May 2025, the Company announced a new share repurchase program of up to $100 billion and raised its quarterly dividend from $0.25 to $0.26 per share. During 2025 it repurchased $89.3 billion of its common stock and paid dividends and dividend equivalents of $15.4 billion.
- The document describes no acquisitions or restructurings. Risk factors highlight artificial intelligence features and expansion into specialized applications such as health and financial services as areas of added regulatory and safety risk.

4. FINANCIAL RED FLAGS
- Gross margin pressure: Products gross margin percentage decreased to 36.8% from 37.2%, due to product mix and tariff costs. Management states that gross margins will generally be subject to volatility and downward pressure.
- Weakness in Greater China: net sales fell 4%, following an 8% decline in the prior year. Wearables, Home and Accessories also declined 4%, following a 7% decline in the prior year.
- Debt and near-term obligations: the Company had $91.3 billion of fixed-rate notes outstanding, with $12.4 billion payable within 12 months. It also had $8.0 billion of commercial paper outstanding, and a deemed repatriation tax payable of $8.8 billion due within 12 months. Manufacturing purchase obligations were $56.2 billion, with $55.4 billion payable within 12 months.
- Liquidity is not a stated concern: cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $132.4 billion, and management believes this is sufficient for the next 12 months and beyond.
- Tax: the lower 2025 effective tax rate reflects a $10.7 billion year-over-year decrease in the provision related to the State Aid Decision, so it is not a recurring improvement. Uncertain tax positions require significant judgment.
- No going-concern warning or accounting restatement appears in the document. New accounting standards (ASU 2025-06, ASU 2024-03, ASU 2023-09) are disclosure or recognition changes still being evaluated or scheduled for later adoption.

10-Q.title: 10-Q  - Quarterly report [Sections 13 or 15(d)]
10-Q.summary:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY – Apple Inc. (AAPL), Form 10-Q for the third quarter of fiscal 2026 (quarter ended June 27, 2026)

1. BUSINESS AND REVENUE PERFORMANCE
- Total net sales (Q3): $109,417 million (+16%); nine months: $364,357 million (+16%)
- iPhone (Q3): $54,252 million (+22%), driven by higher sales of Pro models; nine months: $196,515 million (+22%)
- Services (Q3): $30,739 million (+12%), driven by advertising and cloud services; nine months: $91,728 million (+14%)
- Mac (Q3): $10,352 million (+29%), driven by laptops
- Wearables, Home and Accessories (Q3): $7,883 million (+6%)
- iPad (Q3): $6,191 million (-6%), due to lower sales of iPad mini and iPad Air; nine months: $21,700 million (+3%)
- Regions (Q3): Americas $45,781 million (+11%); Europe $29,395 million (+22%); Greater China $18,816 million (+22%); Japan $6,554 million (+13%); Rest of Asia Pacific $8,871 million (+16%)
- Total gross margin (Q3): $54,770 million; gross margin percentage 50.1% vs 46.5% a year earlier. Products gross margin percentage was 40.1% (vs 34.5%) and Services was 75.6% (flat). The Products improvement came from product mix and tariff refunds, partly offset by higher costs, including memory.
- Operating expenses (Q3): $19,075 million (+23%). R&D was $11,729 million (+32%), driven by AI-related infrastructure costs and headcount. SG&A was $7,346 million (+10%).
- Effective tax rate (Q3): 17.9% vs 16.4% a year earlier

2. THREE KEY RISKS
- Component and compute supply: The Company is experiencing supply constraints and rising costs for advanced semiconductors, NAND and DRAM memory, and expects these trends to intensify. This could materially hurt revenue and gross margin, and price increases may not offset the impact and could reduce demand. The filing also adds a risk around access to sufficient cloud and AI computing capacity, including reliance on third-party cloud providers.
- Regulatory and antitrust pressure: A U.S. court order currently bars the Company from charging commissions on certain purchases, though the Ninth Circuit has instructed the district court to modify the injunction to allow a commission. EU DMA compliance, including interoperability obligations, has been challenged by the Commission, and the DMA provides for significant fines. These requirements have caused the Company not to launch some features, such as Siri AI, in certain jurisdictions. Civil antitrust suits in the U.S. also allege monopolization in smartphone markets.
- Google search licensing and tariffs: Revenue from search licensing with Google is exposed to the Google antitrust remedies, which both the DOJ and Google have appealed. A reversal could bring remedies that prohibit Google from offering Apple commercial terms for search distribution. Separately, tariffs, including new Section 301 tariffs and a possible Section 232 semiconductor action, remain uncertain and could hurt supply chain, pricing and gross margin.

4. FINANCIAL RED FLAGS
- Gross margin outlook: Management believes gross margins will be subject to volatility and downward pressure. Part of the Products margin gain came from tariff refunds, which may not recur, while memory costs are rising.
- Rising costs: R&D grew much faster than net sales (+32% in Q3), reflecting AI investment. R&D was 11% of net sales in Q3 vs 9% a year earlier.
- Purchase obligations: Manufacturing purchase obligations were $57.0 billion, of which $56.2 billion is payable within 12 months. Other purchase obligations were $29.3 billion, with $9.2 billion payable within 12 months.
- Capital return: In Q3 the Company repurchased $25.8 billion of its common stock and paid dividends and dividend equivalents of $4.0 billion. Management states that cash, marketable securities, operating cash flow and debt market access are sufficient for the next 12 months and beyond.
- Tax: The effective tax rate rose in Q3 and in the first nine months (17.6% vs 15.4%).
- No going-concern warnings or changes in critical accounting estimates were reported. Upcoming accounting standards (ASU 2023-09 in Q4 2026, ASU 2024-03 in Q4 2028, ASU 2025-06 in Q1 2029) are disclosure or accounting changes under evaluation.

3. STRATEGIC CHANGES
- Product and software launches: During Q3 the Company announced iOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, iPadOS 27, watchOS 27, visionOS 27 and tvOS 27, and introduced Siri AI.
- AI investment: R&D spending is increasingly directed at AI infrastructure, and the Company relies on both its own data centers and third-party cloud providers for compute.
- Pricing actions: The Company has taken price increases to address component cost pressure.
- Tariff refunds: Following the Supreme Court ruling of February 20, 2026 against certain IEEPA tariffs, the Company has applied for refunds and records them as a reduction of products cost of sales.
- Regulatory adaptation: The Company is changing its App Store and iOS practices in the U.S. and EU (DMA) in response to legal and regulatory requirements.
- No acquisitions or restructurings are mentioned in the document.

10-K.title: 10-K  - Annual report [Section 13 and 15(d), not S-K Item 405]
10-K.summary:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY – Microsoft Corporation (MSFT), Form 10-K, fiscal year ended June 30, 2026

1. BUSINESS AND REVENUE PERFORMANCE
- Revenue: $331,839 million (+18%), driven by growth in Microsoft Cloud
- Gross margin: $225,465 million (+16%)
- Operating income: $155,237 million (+21%)
- Net income: $133,749 million (+31%); diluted EPS: $17.95 (+32%)
- Adjusted net income (non-GAAP, excludes OpenAI gains and losses): $128,786 million (+22%); adjusted diluted EPS: $17.28 (+22%)
- Microsoft Cloud revenue: $214.4 billion (+27%); commercial remaining performance obligation: $678 billion (+84%)
- Productivity and Business Processes: revenue $139,996 million (+16%), operating income $83,879 million (+20%). Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud revenue grew 17%, LinkedIn 11% and Dynamics 365 18%.
- Intelligent Cloud: revenue $137,791 million (+30%), operating income $56,972 million (+28%). Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 41%.
- More Personal Computing: revenue $54,052 million ((1)%), operating income $14,386 million (+2%). XBOX content and services revenue fell 5% and XBOX hardware revenue fell 29%. Search advertising revenue excluding traffic acquisition costs grew 12%.
- Cash from operations: $182.9 billion, up $46.8 billion
- Foreign currency had a favorable impact of 2% on revenue and operating income.

2. THREE KEY RISKS
- AI and cloud infrastructure investments: they will keep raising operating costs and may reduce operating margins. Datacenters depend on land, energy, networking supplies and servers, including GPUs, and some components have very few qualified suppliers.
- Tax dispute with the IRS: the IRS is seeking an additional tax payment of $28.9 billion plus penalties and interest on transfer pricing for tax years 2004 to 2013. Microsoft disagrees and will contest the NOPAs. It considers its allowances for income tax contingencies adequate. Audits for tax years 2014 to 2017 are also ongoing.
- Competition, trade policy and macro conditions: the markets are highly competitive. Tariffs, trade restrictions and geopolitical factors could cause supply chain challenges and cost volatility, and demand is correlated to global macroeconomic factors.

4. FINANCIAL RED FLAGS is covered below after strategic changes.

3. STRATEGIC CHANGES
- OpenAI partnership extended in October 2025 and April 2026. Microsoft is a major investor, continues to receive revenue-sharing payments and holds rights to OpenAI's intellectual property for integration into its products. The fiscal 2026 gains relate primarily to the dilution gain from the OpenAI Recapitalization.
- Continued heavy investment in AI infrastructure, datacenter capacity and AI talent. Additions to property and equipment rose $51.4 billion.
- Metrics and naming updates: Microsoft 365 Consumer subscribers was removed as a metric in the first quarter of fiscal 2026. Search and news advertising was renamed Search advertising, and Gaming was renamed XBOX.
- Impairment and other related expenses in the XBOX business.
- Microsoft 365 Copilot is driving revenue per user growth, and Copilot advertising expenses were higher.

4. FINANCIAL RED FLAGS
- Margin pressure from AI: gross margin percentage decreased slightly, and Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage decreased to 66%. Intelligent Cloud cost of revenue rose 44% against revenue growth of 30%, and its gross margin percentage decreased.
- Large commitments: contractual obligations total $743,821 million, including operating and finance leases of $443,506 million, purchase commitments of $194,060 million, construction commitments of $34,566 million and long-term debt principal of $46,136 million. $241,922 million of the total falls due in fiscal 2027.
- Lower liquidity: cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments were $76.8 billion, versus $94.6 billion a year earlier. Cash used in investing rose $66.9 billion to $139.5 billion. Management still expects liquidity to be sufficient for at least the next 12 months.
- Earnings quality: net income was boosted by OpenAI gains ($6.5 billion of net gains in other income, versus $4.8 billion of net losses a year earlier), and other income (expense), net swung to $10,697 million. Adjusted figures show lower growth than GAAP.
- Other items: XBOX impairment, higher general and administrative expenses (+10%) due to higher legal expenses, and an effective tax rate of 19% versus 18%.
- No going-concern warnings or new accounting changes with material impact are disclosed.

10-Q.title: 10-Q  - Quarterly report [Sections 13 or 15(d)]
10-Q.summary:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY – Microsoft Corporation (MSFT), Form 10-Q, first quarter of fiscal year 2027 (three months ended September 30, 2026)

1. BUSINESS AND REVENUE PERFORMANCE
- Revenue: $92,279 million (+19%), driven by growth in Agents and Infra
- Gross margin: $62,559 million (+17%)
- Operating income: $45,915 million (+21%)
- Net income: $36,629 million (+32%); diluted EPS: $4.92 (+32%)
- Adjusted net income (non-GAAP): $36,422 million (+18%); adjusted diluted EPS (non-GAAP): $4.89 (+18%). These exclude OpenAI investment gains and losses. GAAP net income benefited from net gains on OpenAI investments, versus net losses in the prior-year quarter.
- Commercial remaining performance obligation: $677 billion (+73%)
- Microsoft Cloud revenue: $63.9 billion (+30%)
- Azure revenue: +48% (an increase of $10.8 billion)
- Microsoft 365 commercial cloud: +17%. Commercial seats grew 5%.
- Microsoft 365 consumer cloud: +17%
- Industry solutions cloud: +10%
- Segment Agents and Infra: Revenue $76,795 million (+25%); operating income $40,558 million (+24%)
- Segment Devices and Consumer: Revenue $15,484 million (-3%); operating income $5,357 million (+2%)
  - Search and advertising ex TAC: +12%
  - XBOX content and services: -2%
  - XBOX hardware: -14%
  - Windows OEM and devices: -22%, due to the prior-year Windows 10 end-of-support demand, inventory drawdowns by OEM and channel partners, and weaker PC demand
- Operating expenses: $16,644 million (+6%). Total company headcount decreased 2%.
- Cash from operations: $58.0 billion, up $12.9 billion

2. THREE KEY RISKS
- Margin pressure from AI and cloud buildout: Management says datacenter and device investments will continue to increase operating costs and may decrease operating margins. Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage fell to 66% on mix shift to Azure. Agents and Infra cost of revenue rose 35%.
- Supply chain and infrastructure dependence: Datacenters depend on permitted and buildable land, predictable energy, networking supplies, and servers, including GPUs. Some components have very few qualified suppliers. Tariffs and trade restrictions could raise costs and disrupt supply.
- Tax dispute and competition: The IRS is seeking an additional $28.9 billion plus penalties and interest for tax years 2004 to 2013. The company disagrees and will contest it. Separately, the markets are highly competitive and consumer device demand is weak (Windows OEM and devices -22%).

3. STRATEGIC CHANGES
- New segment structure announced in September 2026: Agents and Infra (applications and agents, multi-model system, Azure infrastructure) and Devices and Consumer. Prior periods were recast.
- Metrics were updated: a new Industry solutions cloud revenue growth metric was created, and the Microsoft 365 commercial seat metric now includes paid GitHub seats. The definitions of Azure, Microsoft 365 commercial cloud, and Search and advertising growth were also adjusted.
- Continued heavy investment in compute capacity, datacenters, and AI training infrastructure. Additions to property and equipment rose by $20.0 billion in the quarter.
- Long-term OpenAI partnership: Microsoft is a major investor, receives revenue-sharing payments, and holds rights to OpenAI's intellectual property.
- Capital return: $2.9 billion of share repurchases (6 million shares), with $37.7 billion remaining of the $60 billion program. Dividends declared were $7.3 billion.

4. FINANCIAL RED FLAGS
- Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments fell to $64.5 billion from $76.8 billion at June 30, 2026. Cash used in investing rose to $42.0 billion and cash used in financing to $16.6 billion, including a $4.9 billion increase in debt repayments. Management still expects liquidity to be sufficient for at least the next 12 months.
- Interest expense was $870 million versus $698 million, driven by higher finance lease interest.
- Adjusted other income (expense), net was $(234) million versus $401 million. Underlying non-operating results worsened, and the GAAP net income increase of 32% is flattered by OpenAI gains versus prior-year losses.
- Agents and Infra operating income percentage decreased slightly on the Azure mix shift. Devices and Consumer operating income growth came from lower amortization of Activision Blizzard intangibles, not from revenue growth.
- The effective tax rate rose to 20% from 19%.
- The IRS dispute ($28.9 billion plus penalties and interest) is a material contingency. Management believes its allowances for income tax contingencies are adequate.
- No going-concern warnings. No new accounting changes beyond the segment and metric changes described above.

10-K.title: 10-K  - Annual report [Section 13 and 15(d), not S-K Item 405]
10-K.summary:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY – Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN), Form 10-K, fiscal year ended December 31, 2025

1. BUSINESS AND REVENUE PERFORMANCE
- Net sales: $716,924 million (+12%), versus $637,959 million in 2024
- North America: $426,305 million (+10%)
- International: $161,894 million (+13%)
- AWS: $128,725 million (+20%). Growth came from higher customer usage, partly offset by pricing changes tied to long-term contracts.
- Operating income: $79,975 million, versus $68,593 million in 2024. By segment: AWS $45,606 million, North America $29,619 million, International $4,750 million.
- Net income: $77,670 million, versus $59,248 million. Diluted EPS: $7.17, versus $5.53.
- Other income (expense), net: $15,229 million, versus $(2,250) million in 2024. The gain came mainly from the Anthropic investment (upward price adjustments and conversion gains).
- Technology and infrastructure expense: $108,521 million (+23%), driven by infrastructure spending including depreciation.
- Operating cash flow: $139,514 million, versus $115,877 million.
- Remaining AWS-related performance obligations on contracts over one year: approximately $244 billion.
- Q1 2026 guidance: net sales between $173.5 billion and $178.5 billion (11% to 15% growth). Operating income between $16.5 billion and $21.5 billion, versus $18.4 billion in Q1 2025.

2. THREE KEY RISKS
- Intense competition and heavy AI investment. The company says competitors, including AI-enabled new entrants, may offer lower prices or devote more resources to technology. Returns on its large AI and infrastructure investments may not meet expectations and could lead to write-downs.
- Regulation and litigation. The company faces open competition, consumer protection and privacy investigations, plus antitrust cases brought by the FTC and state attorneys general. Examples include the Italian competition fine, reduced to €752 million and under appeal, and the Luxembourg data-protection fine of €746 million, also under appeal. The Kove patent case carries a $525 million jury award plus $148 million in pre-judgment interest, under appeal. Losses could exceed amounts recorded.
- Supply chain, trade and tariffs. China-based sellers and suppliers account for significant portions of seller-services and advertising revenue and of components and finished goods. The company also relies on a limited group of semiconductor suppliers, including GPUs for AI. It flags tariff policy and memory-chip supply volatility as factors that could affect results.

3. STRATEGIC CHANGES
- Capital spending on AI infrastructure: cash capital expenditures were $128.3 billion, versus $77.7 billion in 2024. Most of it supports AWS growth, and management expects further increases in 2026.
- Anthropic: the company invested $2.7 billion in convertible notes in 2025. Part of the notes converted to nonvoting preferred stock, and the estimated fair value of the remaining notes was approximately $45.8 billion. A further conversion after year-end is expected to produce gains of approximately $3 billion and approximately $12 billion in Q1 2026.
- Other initiatives: a satellite broadband network (Amazon Leo, with approximately $1 billion of higher year-over-year costs in Q1 2026 guidance), autonomous vehicles for ride-hailing, quick commerce, and sharper prices in international stores.
- Restructuring: approximately $2.7 billion of estimated severance costs for planned role eliminations and approximately $1.3 billion of asset impairments, mainly physical stores.
- Financing: $15.0 billion of senior notes issued in November 2025, and the commercial paper programs increased from $20.0 billion to $30.0 billion.
- Acquisitions in 2025 were immaterial.

4. FINANCIAL RED FLAGS
- Free cash flow fell to $11,194 million from $38,219 million, as capital spending grew faster than operating cash flow.
- Debt and commitments are rising. Long-term debt was $65.6 billion, versus $52.6 billion. Total commitments were $439,661 million, including $96,373 million of leases not yet commenced. Financing activities went from an outflow of $(11,812) million to an inflow of $9,661 million.
- Earnings quality: part of the profit growth comes from non-operating Anthropic gains. These are Level 3 valuations that depend on observable price changes in a private company. The provision for income taxes was $19.1 billion, versus $9.3 billion.
- One-time charges: $2.5 billion for the FTC settlement, severance, impairments and Italian tax-dispute resolution. Other operating expense (income), net was $4,639 million (+508%).
- Accounting estimate change: effective January 1, 2025, the useful life of a subset of servers and networking equipment was shortened from six to five years. This added $1.4 billion of depreciation expense.
- Tax: the auditor flagged uncertain tax positions as a critical audit matter, with $6.6 billion accrued for tax contingencies.
- Q1 2026 operating income guidance is a wide range, and management notes the guidance assumes no additional legal settlements or restructurings.
- No going-concern warning. The auditor issued an unqualified opinion. No borrowings were outstanding under the revolving credit facilities or commercial paper programs, and cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities were $123.0 billion.

10-Q.title: 10-Q  - Quarterly report [Sections 13 or 15(d)]
10-Q.summary:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY – Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN), Form 10-Q, quarter ended June 30, 2026

1. BUSINESS AND REVENUE PERFORMANCE
- Total net sales Q2 2026: $200,606 million (+20%). Q2 2025 was $167,702 million. Six months: $382,125 million (+18%).
- North America: $116,177 million (+16%). Growth came from unit sales (including third-party sellers), advertising and subscriptions.
- International: $42,197 million (+15%).
- AWS: $42,232 million (+37%), driven by higher customer usage and partly offset by pricing changes from long-term contracts.
- Advertising services: $19,809 million, up from $15,694 million. Third-party seller services: $46,780 million. Subscription services: $13,730 million.
- Operating income Q2 2026: $27,461 million, up from $19,171 million. AWS contributed $16,621 million (Q2 2025: $10,160 million), North America $9,123 million and International $1,717 million.
- Net income Q2 2026: $62,647 million (Q2 2025: $18,164 million). Diluted EPS: $5.75 (Q2 2025: $1.68).
- The net income jump was driven mainly by Other income (expense), net of $53,415 million. Of this, $50.5 billion came from upward valuation adjustments to the Anthropic nonvoting preferred stock investment.
- AWS contract backlog: about $496 billion of unrecognized performance obligations, with a weighted-average remaining life of 6.4 years.
- Q3 2026 guidance: net sales of $197.0 billion to $202.0 billion (+9% to +12%), well below the Q2 growth rate. Operating income of $22.5 billion to $26.5 billion, versus $17.4 billion in Q3 2025.

2. THREE KEY RISKS
- Capital intensity and AI infrastructure dependence. Purchases of property and equipment were $54,208 million in Q2, and management expects capex to increase in 2026. The company relies on a limited group of suppliers for semiconductors, including GPUs, and the forward-looking statements flag memory chip supply volatility.
- Concentrated, hard-to-value equity investments. Equity, warrant and convertible debt investments were recorded at $229.7 billion, primarily in Anthropic and OpenAI. They are private-company, Level 3 measurements, and the company says market sensitivities are not practicable to estimate. Declines in value could be written down.
- Litigation, regulation and tax. US antitrust and consumer protection cases (including the FTC) seek billions of dollars in damages. A new Xockets patent investigation at the US International Trade Commission was instituted in June 2026 and covers AWS GB200-based offerings. Tax disputes with India (cloud services fees) and Luxembourg could result in significant payments. Income tax contingencies were approximately $7.1 billion.

3. STRATEGIC CHANGES
- Globalstar acquisition: a merger agreement was signed on April 13, 2026, implying a value of approximately $10.9 billion including debt. Each Globalstar share can elect $90.00 in cash or 0.3210 Amazon shares, with cash elections capped at 40% of shares. Closing is expected in 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and satellite replacement milestones.
- OpenAI: the company invested $15.0 billion in Series C Preferred Stock in Q1 and $13.7 billion in Q2 2026. After quarter-end it funded the remaining $21.3 billion Commitment Amount. The AWS commitment was expanded by $100.0 billion over 8.0 years.
- Anthropic: in Q2 2026 the company invested $5.0 billion in Series G and $5.0 billion in Series H nonvoting preferred stock. The AWS collaboration was expanded by more than $100.0 billion over 10.0 years. A financing facility of up to $20.0 billion was put in place, with $15.0 billion remaining available after the Series H investment.
- Financing the build-out: the company issued Euro, Swiss franc and Canadian dollar notes in 2026 and signed a $17.5 billion delayed draw term loan. After quarter-end it issued a further $25.0 billion of US dollar notes.
- Investment is continuing in AI, the satellite broadband network (costs are largely expensed) and fulfillment network capacity.

4. FINANCIAL RED FLAGS
- Free cash flow was negative on a trailing-twelve-month basis: $(7,604) million, versus $18,184 million a year earlier. Operating cash flow was $161,403 million, but net purchases of property and equipment were $169,007 million.
- Debt rose sharply. Long-term debt was $128,894 million at June 30, 2026, versus $65,648 million at December 31, 2025. Interest expense was $1,314 million in Q2 2026, versus $516 million in Q2 2025. Management expects additional financing in 2026 and warns that higher borrowing could raise costs.
- Earnings quality. Net income was inflated by non-cash investment revaluation gains. Total non-operating income was $53,396 million in Q2 2026, against operating income of $27,461 million. The six-month tax provision of $27.8 billion included $15.9 billion of discrete tax expense tied to the Anthropic gains.
- Large commitments. Total contractual commitments were $650,034 million, including leases not yet commenced of $137,214 million and unconditional purchase obligations of $130,065 million.
- Working capital. Accounts receivable, net and other rose to $88,092 million from $67,729 million at year-end.
- A one-time benefit: about $640 million of IEEPA tariff refunds reduced Q2 cost of sales, and this is not expected to recur. The Q3 guidance assumes no impact from energy derivative remeasurements.
- No going-concern warning and no covenants on the notes. No borrowings were outstanding under the commercial paper programs or the revolving credit facilities. Cash, equivalents and marketable securities were $123.0 billion. Disclosure controls were assessed as effective.
